## Context
Gerrit Verified run 31752047186 spent 100.66-130.59s per Ubuntu cell in `test_bridge_backstop_fires_on_a_uniform_hourly_cadence`. Runtime tracing proves `_bridge_schedule()` reparses the same workflow YAML inside the 1,440-minute comprehension. Local current=7.925s, invariant reuse=0.00106s. The exhaustive cadence proof is valuable; repeated YAML parsing is not. This remediation matches invariant-sharing practice in pytest, Django, and Pylint/Astroid. No prior rejection was found; `coercive-paediatric-bug` rejects added parallelism without aggregate savings, which this does not use.

## Plan
- Strengthen the existing unit test with a behavioral oracle that counts schedule acquisition and requires one acquisition per cadence proof while preserving all 1,440 minute evaluations and exact gap assertion.
- Hoist the immutable schedule value once before the comprehension.
- Run the held-out RED→GREEN and defect-seeded mutation check, the focused policy suite, lint/typecheck, and paired timing runs.
- Land through Gerrit and record observed Ubuntu runner-time savings; back-out is a Gerrit revert restoring the prior comprehension.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] The cadence test still evaluates every one of the 1,440 minutes and asserts uniform 60-minute circular gaps.
- [x] A unit oracle proves workflow schedule acquisition occurs once, fails on the current 1,440-read implementation, and passes after the change.
- [x] Reintroducing schedule acquisition inside the minute loop returns the oracle to RED.
- [x] Paired local timing demonstrates the repeated YAML parsing cost is eliminated without new jobs or reduced coverage.
- [x] Focused tests, lint, typecheck, Gerrit LLM-Review +1, and Gerrit Verified +1 pass before merge.
- [x] The final ticket comment records RED/GREEN/mutation evidence and measured savings.
